This year has officially become the year of the super app. OpenAI recently launched its own super app and even admitted that the app was "a bit of a mess." Meanwhile, Microsoft's CEO has also confirmed that a Copilot super app is on the way.

Microsoft Copilot "Super App" to combine Cowork, chat, coding, and more

Microsoft is developing an AI "super app" that combines Copilot chat, coding, and intelligent agent capabilities. Speaking during Wednesday's earnings call, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said the app would launch this year and cover "consumer and commercial experiences." Nadella said: "Copilot is rapidly evolving from chat to Cowork to Autopilots. This quarter, we'll bring these Copilot experiences, including coding capabilities, together into a single super app... This is a significant step forward, and I look forward to sharing more details with you later."

OpenAI's own rollout of its "super app" has already been a complete mess, but that clearly hasn't deterred other companies from continuing to pursue the super app strategy.

Microsoft may well be better positioned to deliver an all-in-one app without repeating OpenAI's missteps.

That said, CEO Satya Nadella has also recently stated that the company is gradually shifting away from apps and toward a focus on intelligent agents. The AI era is still very new, and the trends and best practices for building AI-centric interfaces are still constantly evolving.

On Apple's side, there is no indication whatsoever of a shift toward the super app direction; instead, the company continues to launch new apps that are standalone and specialised. It will be interesting to see whether this approach changes down the road.

What are your thoughts on this round of "super app" hype? Feel free to share with us in the comments section.
